title: Chapter III

teacherSummary.text: Nick receives a formal invitation to one of Gatsby's parties, where hundreds of uninvited guests drink, dance and gossip about the host. With Jordan he meets the owl-eyed man in the library, amazed that the books are real. Nick talks with a young man who turns out to be Gatsby, with his reassuring smile and 'old sport.' Gatsby speaks privately with Jordan. Leaving, guests see a car wreck in the ditch. Nick describes his own ordinary life and his friendship with Jordan, who lies and is a careless driver.

segments.script: During Prohibition (1920–1933) alcohol flowed at private parties; jazz orchestras, cocktails and new dances were features of the age. The party presents Gatsby through rumour and spectacle before revealing the man, and links carelessness (driving, honesty) to the novel's moral concerns. Characterization: Gatsby's smile, "one of those rare smiles with a quality of eternal reassurance in it," and his formal "old sport." Irony: Guests gossip about Gatsby (he killed a man, he was a German spy) while drinking his liquor. Watch for the green light: The light at the end of Daisy's dock: Gatsby's dream, distant and unreachable, and finally the "orgiastic future" that recedes before everyone. In this chapter: “of faces and voices and colour under the constantly changing light” (Chapter III, paragraph 5).
